answer.original_source: Wendell Weeks, Corning Chairman, CEO and President, quoted by Fox News Digital on 2026-07-01
answer.new_information: The record is a Corning CEO quote (2026-07-01, period stated only as 'over the coming years', no numeric base year) that the company will probably double in size and that almost all new hires will be in advanced manufacturing. It is not an NVIDIA disclosure and carries no NVDA-specific number. The Corning-NVIDIA three-facility project (more than 3,000 jobs in North Carolina and Texas, tenfold US optical capacity, 'earlier this year', no completion date) and the Wistron Texas AI-supercomputer manufacturing item (no jobs figure, no date) appear only as Fox News reporting with no named primary source, so they are relayed context, not independently verified. The Corning planning supervisor's quote on AI demand is a qualitative statement. No stored questions, catalog entries or stored pieces were supplied, so no existing argument can be updated or compared.
answer.reason: Nothing in the record moves a stored number, probability or risk because no questions or pieces were supplied. It is a supplier-side pickup (Corning, not NVDA) with a CEO growth statement that has no period or base, and the NVIDIA partnership details are unattributed third-party relays of an earlier announcement. It does not carry an investment judgement that a catalog question lacks, and it is not ambiguous enough to be unresolved. The NVIDIA-Corning facilities and the Wistron Texas operations would need NVIDIA's own disclosure or a dated filing before they could bear on an NVDA argument.
